Alternatively, Astral Stair and its Hyper version can both be unlocked in the
A highway used to reach other worlds and dimensions. It's dangerous to venture through alone, but you probably won't listen to me anyway, will you?
Enemies grow stronger over time, gaining +10% Max Health and +0.1% Movement Speed every minute. This effect stacks with
Enemies on Astral Stair follow the beat of the music and turn either red or blue. They can only be damaged by weapons of the same color they're currently "wearing".
Astral Stair is home to special boss enemies,
Cosmic Eggs, which can cast the same
ability the player can normally obtain. It halves the player's health at every cast, making it potentially dangerous even to characters with high stat bonuses.

On stage start, the player will be standing on a floating platform, and unable to move. The platform will disappear within a few seconds, and the player will plummet through a mysterious abyss, landing in a vertical hallway. This cutscene will auto-skip after all relics in the stage have been obtained. This is the main hub of the map. Astral Stair is somewhat unintuitive to traverse compared to other maps. The map is static, but makes use of teleportation "doors" which jump the player between predetermined points. Successfully recovering the relics requires finding and using these doors. The doorways at the very top/bottom of this hallway jump the player to the other end of it. Doorways along the left and right sides of this hallway jump to the smaller rooms to the left/right. Tips:

"Doors" are large, dark wood areas in the wall, which may be difficult to distinguish from regular stage wall/background until the player learns what to look for. They always have the same shape/size/design. They are always facing the camera (minus the bottommost door).
Walk (up) into the middle of a door to teleport. Upon teleporting the player will "land" at the counterpart door. Walk (up) into this one to return to the door prior to it.
Door pairing is static: any two doors only teleport between each other. This makes stage navigation very predictable and easy once players get a handle on it.

The smaller rooms to the sides vary in contents and number. In general, players traverse 2-3 smaller rooms, proceeding in one direction, until reaching a room containing a relic or stage item. Backtracking to the main hallway is accomplished by retracing one's steps.
Alternatively, destroying the terrain such as with
can allow the player to roam the map more freely.
